businessDrawNeedWeight.citation: An owner short of money takes more of the month's profit (JPMorgan Chase Institute, small business cash flows 2016-2019).

spread.citation: An owner short of money takes more of the month's profit (JPMorgan Chase Institute, small business cash flows 2016-2019).

businessDrawKeepWeight.citation: An owner keeps profit in a business whose cash is below a few months of payroll (JPMorgan Chase Institute: median small business holds 27 days of cash).

spread.citation: An owner keeps profit in a business whose cash is below a few months of payroll (JPMorgan Chase Institute: median small business holds 27 days of cash).

businessDrawSizeWeight.citation: Owners smooth draws rather than take everything (IRS SOI sole proprietor and S-corporation distributions against net income).

spread.citation: Owners smooth draws rather than take everything (IRS SOI sole proprietor and S-corporation distributions against net income).

businessCushionMonths.citation: Median small business cash buffer of about one month (JPMorgan Chase Institute 2016).

spread.citation: Median small business cash buffer of about one month (JPMorgan Chase Institute 2016).

businessFoundBaseline.citation: How far starting a business sits below not starting one before room, traits and losing work; checked against BDS 2023 establishment entry rates (about 9 percent a year).

spread.citation: How far starting a business sits below not starting one before room, traits and losing work; checked against BDS 2023 establishment entry rates (about 9 percent a year).

businessFoundRoomWeight.citation: Room in a market (incumbents' demand above their capacity) draws entrants (Census BDS entry rises with local demand growth).

spread.unit: score per share of unmet demand
spread.citation: Room in a market (incumbents' demand above their capacity) draws entrants (Census BDS entry rises with local demand growth).

businessFoundUnemployedWeight.citation: Losing a job pushes some toward starting a business (Fairlie 2013, necessity entrepreneurship).

spread.citation: Losing a job pushes some toward starting a business (Fairlie 2013, necessity entrepreneurship).

businessStartupMonthsOfCosts.citation: Startup capital of a few months of operating costs (Kauffman Firm Survey: median startup capital about 30,000 dollars for employer firms).

spread.citation: Startup capital of a few months of operating costs (Kauffman Firm Survey: median startup capital about 30,000 dollars for employer firms).

businessStartupTermMonths.citation: SBA microloans run up to six years; 7(a) working capital loans up to ten. Five years is within both.

businessFounderMinimumAge.citation: Kauffman: most new business owners are 25 to 64.

businessFounderMaximumAge.citation: Kauffman: most new business owners are 25 to 64.

businessExpandBaseline.citation: How far opening another location sits below not opening one before room, traits and the books; to be checked against BDS 2023 establishment births less firm startups (new locations of existing firms).

spread.citation: How far opening another location sits below not opening one before room, traits and the books; to be checked against BDS 2023 establishment births less firm startups (new locations of existing firms).

businessExpandStrengthWeight.citation: Owners with cash well above their cushion are the ones able to fund a location; thin ones are not (JPMorgan Chase Institute small business cash buffers).

spread.unit: score per unit of cash strength (cash less cushion over cash plus cushion)
spread.citation: Owners with cash well above their cushion are the ones able to fund a location; thin ones are not (JPMorgan Chase Institute small business cash buffers).

businessCountedFoundBaseline.citation: One adult's monthly pull toward founding an employer business, before room, prospect, capital, traits and losing work, summed over the wider population. Set so a steady town's establishments grow about as fast as real net establishment growth while exits are rare (Absecon, 2021-2023: 2 openings among 27 businesses); gross churn needs voluntary closure. Checked against Census BDS 2023 entry and exit rates.

spread.citation: One adult's monthly pull toward founding an employer business, before room, prospect, capital, traits and losing work, summed over the wider population. Set so a steady town's establishments grow about as fast as real net establishment growth while exits are rare (Absecon, 2021-2023: 2 openings among 27 businesses); gross churn needs voluntary closure. Checked against Census BDS 2023 entry and exit rates.

businessFoundProspectWeight.citation: An entrant weighs an equal share of the market's margin against what they earn now, in log terms (owners' business income against wages: Hamilton 2000; Census Annual Business Survey).

spread.unit: score per log of prospect over income
spread.citation: An entrant weighs an equal share of the market's margin against what they earn now, in log terms (owners' business income against wages: Hamilton 2000; Census Annual Business Survey).

businessProspectIncomeFloorShare.citation: Someone without work weighs a business's prospect against a fraction of the place's median pay, not against nothing.

spread.citation: Someone without work weighs a business's prospect against a fraction of the place's median pay, not against nothing.

businessFoundCapitalWeight.citation: Founders without the money to start weigh against it: most new employer firms start on the owner's savings and small loans (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey, startup report 2023; Census Annual Business Survey, sources of startup capital).

spread.unit: score per log of costs over reach
spread.citation: Founders without the money to start weigh against it: most new employer firms start on the owner's savings and small loans (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey, startup report 2023; Census Annual Business Survey, sources of startup capital).

businessFounderLoanIncomeMultiple.citation: What lenders will advance a founder, in years of the founder's income (SBA 7(a) and microloan practice ties a startup loan to the owner's income and personal guarantee).

spread.citation: What lenders will advance a founder, in years of the founder's income (SBA 7(a) and microloan practice ties a startup loan to the owner's income and personal guarantee).

businessUnionDuesShare.citation: Union dues run about one to two percent of a member's pay or a few hours' pay a month (union constitutions and LM-2 reports); applied to the place's median wage.

spread.citation: Union dues run about one to two percent of a member's pay or a few hours' pay a month (union constitutions and LM-2 reports); applied to the place's median wage.

businessOldestFirmYears.citation: A cap on the oldest opening business's age; a few U.S. small businesses are a century old.

spread.citation: A cap on the oldest opening business's age; a few U.S. small businesses are a century old.

businessGroundwaterOutputElasticity.citation: USDA Economic Research Service, Irrigation & Water Use (2023): irrigated farms are 28% of farms but 54% of crop sales; crop yields fall less than in proportion to irrigation water cut (deficit-irrigation response studies, about 0.3 to 0.6).

spread.unit: share of output lost per share of water cut
spread.citation: USDA Economic Research Service, Irrigation & Water Use (2023): irrigated farms are 28% of farms but 54% of crop sales; crop yields fall less than in proportion to irrigation water cut (deficit-irrigation response studies, about 0.3 to 0.6).

businessComplianceShareOfCosts.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Pollution Abatement Costs and Expenditures: 2005 (MA200(05)): manufacturers spent $20.7 billion operating pollution abatement, about 0.4% of their costs; stricter nonattainment rules weigh more (Greenstone 2002, JPE).
businessComplianceShareOfCosts.estimatedFrom: Twice the manufacturing average abatement operating share, for a binding plan in a nonattainment county.

spread.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Pollution Abatement Costs and Expenditures: 2005 (MA200(05)): manufacturers spent $20.7 billion operating pollution abatement, about 0.4% of their costs; stricter nonattainment rules weigh more (Greenstone 2002, JPE).

businessCloseBaseline.citation: Census BDS 2010-2019, 2022-2023: about 8 to 9% of establishments exit a year (0.7% a month), with forced closures and owners leaving no successor counted on top; checked against the state's exit rate.

spread.unit: logit of a month's closing pull
spread.citation: Census BDS 2010-2019, 2022-2023: about 8 to 9% of establishments exit a year (0.7% a month), with forced closures and owners leaving no successor counted on top; checked against the state's exit rate.

businessCloseLossWeight.citation: Firms that keep losing money exit: exit hazard rises steeply with losses (Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda 2013); checked against BDS exits in a test, never used to pick who closes.

spread.unit: pull per month of revenue lost (decayed over the memory window)
spread.citation: Firms that keep losing money exit: exit hazard rises steeply with losses (Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda 2013); checked against BDS exits in a test, never used to pick who closes.

businessCloseAgeWeight.citation: Owners close or sell as they age out: half of small-business owners are 55 or older (SBA Office of Advocacy 2023), and exits rise past retirement age.

spread.citation: Owners close or sell as they age out: half of small-business owners are 55 or older (SBA Office of Advocacy 2023), and exits rise past retirement age.

businessCloseAgeYears.citation: A decade: the span the age weight is read over (ten years).

businessStartupStaff.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Dynamics Statistics (press release, Sept. 20, 2017): the nation's 414,000 startup firms of 2015 created 2.5 million jobs, about six each.
businessStartupStaff.estimatedFrom: Jobs created by age-0 firms divided by the number of age-0 firms; a founding plans a business of about that size, smaller when the founder's money and loan reach less.

spread.citation: Census BDS age-0 firms: about 5 to 8 jobs per startup across 2002-2023 (3.3 million jobs from 524,000 startups a year in 2002-2006; 2.5 million from 414,000 in 2015).

businessFounderReserveMonths.citation: A founder keeps a few months of living costs and puts the rest of their savings in (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey 2023: owners' personal funds are the most common startup financing; a three-month emergency reserve is the common guidance, CFPB).

spread.unit: months of the founder's living costs
spread.citation: A founder keeps a few months of living costs and puts the rest of their savings in (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey 2023; CFPB emergency savings guidance).

businessDrawSurplusWeight.citation: Owners take out profit the business doesn't need: pass-through owners distribute most of their net income (IRS SOI S-corporation returns: distributions are the bulk of shareholders' net income), keeping a cash cushion (JPMorgan Chase Institute 2016).

spread.citation: IRS SOI S-corporation distributions against net income; JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Is King (2016).

businessCloseStayBar.citation: An owner stays unless the causes add up: most establishments that exit are young or losing money (Census BDS 2010-2023; Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda 2013). Totals are checked against the state's BDS exit rate in a test only.

spread.unit: summed pull a counted owner needs before any pull to close
spread.citation: An owner stays unless the causes add up: most establishments that exit are young or losing money (Census BDS 2010-2023; Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda 2013). Totals are checked against the state's BDS exit rate in a test only.

businessCloseRampWidth.citation: The pull above the stay bar slides to certainty over this span, so nothing flips at the bar; an owner's decision is gradual (Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda 2013).

spread.unit: pull from the stay bar to a sure closing
spread.citation: The pull above the stay bar slides to certainty over this span, so nothing flips at the bar; an owner's decision is gradual (Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda 2013).

businessCloseRunwayWeight.citation: Cash runway drives exits of businesses that are losing money: a median small business holds about 27 days of cash (JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Is King 2016).

spread.unit: pull for a business with no cash cover that is losing money
spread.citation: Cash runway drives exits of businesses that are losing money: a median small business holds about 27 days of cash (JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Is King 2016).

businessCloseRunwayMonths.citation: JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Is King (2016): the median small business holds about 27 cash buffer days.
businessCloseRunwayMonths.estimatedFrom: 27 buffer days, about one month of costs.

spread.citation: JPMorgan Chase Institute, Cash Is King (2016): buffers range from under two weeks to about two months across industries.

businessCloseConditionsWeight.citation: A business that cannot meet its payroll is in distress, a strong exit predictor (Census Small Business Pulse / Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey 2023: firms behind on payments close far more often).

spread.unit: pull per month of payroll it could not pay
spread.citation: A business that cannot meet its payroll is in distress, a strong exit predictor (Census Small Business Pulse / Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey 2023: firms behind on payments close far more often).

businessLossMemoryMonths.citation: Owners judge a business over its annual accounts (IRS Schedule C / Form 1120-S are filed yearly).
businessLossMemoryMonths.estimatedFrom: A year of books, so a loss counts for about a year and then fades.

spread.citation: Small businesses judge viability over six months to two years (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey 2023 reports on 12-month performance).

businessComplianceInPartShare.citation: U.S. EPA Green Book: a nonattainment area designated in part covers only part of the county.
businessComplianceInPartShare.estimatedFrom: Half the weight of a whole-county designation for a business somewhere in the county.

spread.unit: share of a whole-county compliance duty
spread.citation: U.S. EPA Green Book county designations (whole or part); partial areas are commonly the urbanized part of a county.

businessDataPrivacyShareOfCosts.citation: California Department of Finance, Standardized Regulatory Impact Assessment of the CCPA regulations (August 2019): initial compliance about $55 billion, about 1.8% of 2018 California gross state product; the yearly cost after setup is lower.
businessDataPrivacyShareOfCosts.estimatedFrom: Somewhat over half of the first-year share of output, taken as a yearly share of a business's other operating costs once the setup is done.

spread.citation: California Department of Finance, Standardized Regulatory Impact Assessment of the CCPA regulations (August 2019): about 1.8% of 2018 California gross state product in the first year.

businessAgeVerificationShareOfCosts.citation: Age verification vendors price by the check (publicly listed vendor rates run from about $0.10 to $1.00 per verified age); Utah SB 152 (2023) and Louisiana Act 456 (2023) require a platform to verify every new account holder's age.
businessAgeVerificationShareOfCosts.estimatedFrom: A platform's yearly new-account checks at the middle vendor rate, as a share of the telecommunications and online employer's other operating costs.

spread.citation: Vendor rate range per check against the other operating costs of a small online employer.
